svg.text: Beginner • Exam-style revision • Learn the logic, read the evidence, avoid false conclusions
BIG PICTURE | Follow the evidence in order
Statistical significance is not proof of a hypothesis; correlation is not proof of cause.
Blue = concepts • Green = process • Orange = warning • Purple = memory aid

text.tspan: H₀: true accuracy = 50% | H₁: accuracy > 50%
100 coin predictions; observed = 57 correct.
X ~ Binomial(100, 0.5); ask: how surprising is 57+?
Expected correct: E[X] = np → 50% gives 50; 60% gives 60 (n=100).
Power = chance of rejecting H₀ when H₀ is false.
Type I = false positive; Type II = false negative.

svg.text: more data → less overlap → easier to distinguish

text.tspan: H₀: β₁ = β₂ = … = βₖ = 0
H₁: at least one tested coefficient is nonzero.
Small F-test P-value → features jointly improve on a
mean-only baseline. It does NOT prove every feature matters.

svg.text: FWER = P(at least one Type I error)

text.tspan: More tests → more chances to get a false positive by luck.

svg.text: MEMORY AID: divide α by m

text.tspan: Lowers false-positive risk across tests; stricter cutoff can
also lower power, so real effects are easier to miss.
A relationship may predict Y without explaining what changes Y.
Do not assume changing X will change Y without a causal mechanism.

svg.text: CDF(x) = P(X ≤ x); upper tail: P(X ≥ k) = 1 − P(X ≤ k−1)
P-value = tail probability assuming H₀; it is NOT the probability that H₀ is true.
Type I: reject true H₀ = false positive
Type II: miss a false H₀ = false negative
Correlation = association • Causation = X changes Y

text.tspan: Temperature → ice-cream sales + swimming/drownings.
Population → accident + “John” counts.
Market demand → factories + chip sales.
Study time ↔ scores; support calls ↔ satisfaction may reverse.

svg.text: SOURCE FLAGS — DO NOT SILENTLY RECONCILE

text.tspan: • 10 tests: formula gives 40.1%; transcript also says
“about 50%.” [S3]
• Fair-coin cutoff: 58 vs 59 wording is ambiguous. [S1]
• “Variance 10 / SD √10” seems inconsistent with binomial setup;
source cannot resolve transcription vs modeling. [S2]
• Rain/temperature mechanisms are proposed; no general answer. [S4]

svg.text: Answer first; then check the separate answer key below.
1 State H₀ and H₁ in the coin-prediction example.
2 Why is 57/100 not significant at α = 0.05?
3 Define Type I and Type II errors.
4 Why can n = 1,000 improve statistical power?
5 What does the regression F-test evaluate jointly?
6 For 10 tests, compute the Bonferroni threshold.
7 Name two explanations for correlation without causation.
8 Why may ice-cream sales predict drownings without causing them?
3 Type I: false positive; Type II: false negative.
4 Larger n reduces overlap between the hypotheses.
5 Whether tested feature coefficients are jointly zero.
8 Temperature can raise both sales and swimming activity.
ARROWS: big-picture arrows = workflow; X → Y / Z → {X,Y} = proposed causal direction.
SOURCE TAGS: [S1] Python test • [S2] power/sample size • [S3] F-test/multiple testing • [S4] correlation/causation
